item.text: The scan path is contained in `scan/base.go`: `scanPorts` passes the destination list to `execPortsScan`, which expects `ip:port` strings. I also found tests for wildcard address expansion and duplicate ports; the current destination assembly iterates a map, so its output order can vary.

/bin/bash -lc "cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
Progress: Traced the port scan path and existing tests. No project source or tests changed.
Diagnosis: scan/base.go detectScanDest currently accumulates address->ports, expands wildcard addresses, flattens to []string, then deduplicates string pairs. Its map iteration makes output order unstable. scanPorts passes that slice to execPortsScan, which dials each ip:port string and returns successful strings to updatePortStatus/findPortScanSuccessOn. The direct consumer requiring adaptation is execPortsScan; downstream status matching can retain its []string success representation if the scanner flattens the new map locally.
Relevant tests: scan/base_test.go Test_detectScanDest covers empty, single, duplicate, multiple addresses, wildcard. Expectations need map type and additional same-IP multi-port/overlap cases. Existing scan status tests assert wildcard and address matching.
Fix behavior: return initialized empty map when no destinations; expand * over IPv4Addrs into real IP keys; deduplicate ports per IP, including overlap with explicit entries; sort each port slice deterministically; iterate IP keys in stable order before dialing if scan/status order matters. No source edits made under fault-localization role.
EOF"

item.text:
I traced the change to [scan/base.go](/app/scan/base.go:743). `detectScanDest` already collects ports by address, but then flattens them into `ip:port` strings. Its map iteration also makes the resulting order unpredictable.

The direct caller, `scanPorts`, passes that result to `execPortsScan` at [scan/base.go](/app/scan/base.go:787). A fix should pass the new map there, deduplicate and sort each IP’s port slice, expand `*` across configured IPv4 addresses, and return an initialized empty map when there are no destinations. The scanner can still return successful `ip:port` strings for the existing status matching code. The cases to update and extend are in [scan/base_test.go](/app/scan/base_test.go:280).

**No project source or tests were edited.** This pass was restricted to fault localization, so the requested refactor remains outstanding. I recorded the findings in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`.
